messages:
anika: getting a SLO alert — p99 latency for inference gateway in eu-west-1 just spiked, customers seeing 502/504 and timeouts. alert window started ~20:14 UTC. anyone oncall?
ops-bot: SLO Alert: api.gateway.p99 >= 1200ms in eu-west-1. triggered at 2025-03-15T20:14:03Z. related metrics: 502_rate ↑ 4.8x, handshake_timeouts ↑ 10x. Pager: @eng-oncall.
kevin: on it. first glance — probe dashboards show a sudden jump in handshake durations for upstream pool gp-infer-02, while probe success rate dropped ~15%.
maria: support says three customers opened tickets complaining about timeouts and retries, one included logs showing repeated "upstream handshake timeout" in the client. ticket ids: #C-1123, #C-1124, #C-1125.
kevin: can we get logs for a window 20:10-20:20 UTC. running Loki query: ```{job="api-gateway", region="eu-west-1"} |= "handshake timeout" | line_format "{time} {pod} {msg}"```
ops-bot: Query returned 1.2k matches in that window across 6 pods. Top pod: api-gw-02f6 (15% of matches).
anika: traces seem sparse for that window — Jaeger shows <2% sample for gateway traces in eu-west-1 during the spike. could be sampling or instrumentation gap. anyone changed sampling?
kevin: I didn't touch sampling. checking deploy history... there was an automated rollout earlier today of the rate-limiter config at 19:58 UTC (auto canary). It bumped burst_limit for public tier. Not sure why it'd affect handshake timeouts but it's the only config change.
maria: support forwarded an app-level stacktrace showing repeated 503 from our gateway and an upstream 504. customer says retries pile up then they hit client-side timeout.
kevin: hypothesis: sudden client concurrency + increased upstream queueing -> backend prefetch/pool exhaustion -> handshake timeouts. need to confirm with queue_length and connection_pool metrics. running quick MQL: metric(api.upstream.queue_length) by pod for gp-infer-* in eu-west-1 between 20:00-20:20
ops-bot: MQL results: gp-infer-02 shows queue_length spike from 10 -> 120 around 20:12. connection_open_failures also increased.
anika: good catch. any trace IDs around 20:12 that made it through? I only see a handful; sampling might have dropped important spans. we should temporarily increase trace sampling to 100% for the gateway in eu-west-1 to capture repro.
elevated: kevin: doing that now — toggling sampling to 100% for service=api-gateway region=eu-west-1. also enabling DEBUG for handshake path (limited retention).
maria: created internal ticket INF-765 with customer refs and linked the SLO alert. I've asked support to tell customers we're investigating and to collect one request-id from them.
kevin: with sampling on, I see traces showing long TCP connect delays to gp-infer-02 instances (~700-900ms) and multiple retransmits. network metrics show increased packet loss on the host NIC for that node pool around the same time.
anika: is this limited to gp-infer-02 or multi-pool?
ops-bot: gp-infer-02 nodes show NIC drop rate spikes; gp-infer-01 and gp-infer-03 are normal.
kevin: looks like a node-level network degradation. plan: cordon suspected nodes in gp-infer-02, shift traffic, and restart pods. I'll start a controlled drain of api-gw pods hitting that pool and trigger autoscale fallback.
maria: letting customers know we'll fail traffic away from that pool and expect mitigation in ~15min.
anika: capture final checklist: (1) increase sampling for 30m — done, (2) cordon/drain problematic nodes in gp-infer-02 — in progress, (3) review rate-limiter rollout for correlation — noted, (4) add a temporary metric alert for node NIC drop rate to catch recurrence — created.
kevin: cordon + drain completed, restarted 4 pods, p99 latency back down to baseline within 5m. 502/504 rate reduced. I'll open a follow-up RCA to track root cause (hardware vendor reported intermittent NIC firmware bug suspected).
maria: customers updated; support to keep cases open until RCA posted.
anika: closing oncall thread — created incident INC-2025-0315 and assigned to eng-infra for deeper packet capture and to vendor for NIC firmware investigation. thanks all. :white_check_mark:
